comparison: Both evaluate single-cell sequencing and cell type identification (C18-C20). OpenEval finds methodology sound with appropriate clustering. Peer reviewers affirm the single-cell transcriptomic analysis as 'compelling evidence.' Both SUPPORTED, strong agreement.

Both address differential gene expression analysis in diabetes (C21-C26). OpenEval finds claims supported by volcano plots and GO analysis. Peer reviewers affirm findings of 'decreased expression of genes associated with collagen or extracellular matrix organization and angiogenesis.' Both SUPPORTED, strong agreement.

Both evaluate LBH as pericyte marker (C27-C35). OpenEval finds multiple lines of evidence supporting specificity and validation. However, peer review shows disagreement: while two reviewers affirmed LBH as marker, one strongly disputed specificity, claiming 'LBH clearly stained for SMCs, not pericytes' and 'clearly stains endothelial cells.' OpenEval SUPPORTED vs. Peer UNCERTAIN - significant disagreement on marker specificity.

Both address limitations of LBH marker (C74-C75). OpenEval views acknowledgment of limitations as strengthening conclusions. Peer review's UNCERTAIN evaluation incorporates these limitations alongside the specificity concerns. Partial overlap with broader marker evaluation.

Both evaluate pericyte dysfunction analysis in diabetes (C37-C43). OpenEval finds convergence of computational and experimental evidence strongly supportive. Peer reviewers affirm findings about pericyte role in angiogenesis, adhesion, and migration, and reduced interactions in diabetes. Both SUPPORTED, strong agreement.

Both evaluate therapeutic efficacy of LBH (C44-C49). OpenEval finds multiple experimental approaches with adequate statistical power support claims. Peer reviewers affirm therapeutic findings and note 'All my concerns have been properly addressed.' Both SUPPORTED, strong agreement.

Both evaluate human tissue validation (C50-C54). OpenEval finds translation from mouse to human strengthened by appropriate controls and consistent findings. Peer reviewers explicitly support use of 'single-cell transcriptomic analysis in both mouse and human cavernous tissues.' Both SUPPORTED, strong agreement.

Both evaluate protein interaction findings (C55-C60). OpenEval finds rigorous experimental approach with co-IP, LC-MS/MS, and validation. Peer reviewers affirm 'role of LBH and its interactions with other proteins (CRYAB and VIM)' and their involvement in neurovascular regeneration. Both SUPPORTED, strong agreement.

Both evaluate diabetes model characterization (C69-C73). OpenEval finds appropriate characterization with standard protocol. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns, with one noting 'All my concerns have been properly addressed.' Both SUPPORTED, agreement.
